[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Channel keys[/color][/head]
These are the prefixes for the main channels. You can only use the ones your headset is keyed for.
- [color=#684871]Imperial (DSM)[/color] command net uses [color=#6ab7d6]:i[/color], and the Imperial civilian net uses [color=#6ab7d6]:j[/color]. - [color=#bf4d00]NCWL[/color] uses [color=#6ab7d6]:o[/color]. - [color=#535961]Shinohara (SHI)[/color] uses [color=#6ab7d6]:w[/color]. - [color=#ff7f7f]Gorlex / Federation (TFCF)[/color] uses [color=#6ab7d6]:p[/color]. Its member companies have their own nets, such as Cyberdawn on [color=#6ab7d6]:2[/color], Interdyne on [color=#6ab7d6]:3[/color], and SAW on [color=#6ab7d6]:x[/color]. - [bold]Command[/bold] channels are restricted to officers and leaders. The NCWL command net uses [color=#6ab7d6]:h[/color], and it is keyed only into command headsets.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Radio discipline[/color][/head]
- [color=#d9776c]The enemy cannot hear your faction net[/color], but a captured or looted enemy headset can. Watch what you say if your gear falls into enemy hands. - Keep the net clear during a fight. Short, clear callouts about positions, targets, and casualties save lives, while idle chatter gets people killed. - Report enemy movement, request support, and confirm orders. A quiet radio in a warzone usually means something has gone wrong.
